summary.title: The Past Is Not Past: Memory-Enhanced Dynamic Reward Shaping

details: RLVR training of LLMs collapses into narrow, stereotyped behaviors, repeatedly reproducing the same failure mode; entropy regularization only injects randomness under the current policy and does not discourage recurrent error patterns across rollouts.

MEDS: a memory-enhanced dynamic reward shaping framework that maintains a per-prompt memory of past erroneous rollouts and subtracts a penalty from the reward that grows with how frequently a rollout's failure pattern has recurred.

Recurrence is measured at the representation level: layer-wise logits at the first token of the final answer (reused from the forward pass, no extra cost) form a compact 'logic feature' vector; density-based clustering (HDBSCAN) over the memory gives cluster sizes, and the penalty is min(alpha*log(|C_k|+1), beta).
Accompanied by a proof that a monotone penalty on repeated errors yields non-decreasing expected task reward under a KL-regularized policy update.
Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-8B (reasoning) and Qwen2.5-Math-7B (non-reasoning), trained with verl on DAPO-Math-17K merged with MATH levels 3-5, Qwen-Math prompt template.
Built on top of DAPO: batch of 512 prompts, 16 rollouts/prompt, max response 7168 tokens (3072 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B), Adam lr 1e-6, H200 GPUs.

Memory stores only incorrect samples; features = concatenated logits from last 14 layers with L2 normalization; HDBSCAN with min cluster size 2, min samples 1, Euclidean distance; alpha/beta = 0.1/0.2 (1.7B, Math-7B) and 0.02/0.04 (8B); first epoch used only for memory formation.
Baselines: untuned base model, GRPO (KL 1e-3), DAPO (clip 0.2/0.28, no KL), and GRPO with per-token entropy advantage bonus.
Five math benchmarks: AIME24, AMC23, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench; n=128 samples, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0; report pass@1 through pass@128.
Exploration analysis: LLM-judged Within-Step and Across-Step rollout diversity (Claude-Haiku-4.5, 1,600 rollout groups; 21 step-interval pairs) plus Top-1 Eigen Ratio of stored-logit covariance.
Clustering validity: 800 sampled wrong responses labeled by Claude into 11 manually distilled error categories; pairwise agreement between LLM clusters and logit clusters used as correlation metric.
Feature-construction ablation on Qwen2.5-Math-7B: last 14 vs all 28 layers, raw vs adjacent-layer differences, and a degenerate single-cluster variant.

KL-regularized one-step policy update with Gibbs-form optimizer; penalty c(y) monotone in repetition count, assumed anti-correlated with task reward; result follows from a covariance/Chebyshev rearrangement argument giving J(q2) >= J(q1).

key_findings.finding: Penalizing recurrent error clusters via a historical memory consistently improves both greedy and exploratory accuracy over DAPO, GRPO and entropy-based exploration.
key_findings.evidence: Across five math benchmarks and three base models MEDS gives the best overall averages, with gains up to 4.13 pass@1 and 4.37 pass@128 points; largest single-dataset pass@128 gain on Qwen3-8B from 70.81 to 82.67 (+17% relative), and pass@k curves dominate baselines for k in 1..128.

key_findings.finding: Layer-wise logits at the final-answer token are a usable proxy for reasoning structure, not just for the final answer string.
key_findings.evidence: Logit-based clustering agrees with Claude-Haiku-4.5 error-category annotations on 61.2% of sampled response pairs (vs 45.16% for a degenerate single-cluster baseline); case study shows responses with identical wrong answer 1342 land in different clusters while different answers with shared reasoning share a cluster.

key_findings.finding: Better clustering quality translates monotonically into better downstream RL performance, confirming the mechanism rather than a generic regularization effect.
key_findings.evidence: Ranking of Claude-agreement across feature variants (last-14 layers 61.2% > 28-layer diff/14-layer diff ~52-55% ≈ 28 layers 53.87% > single cluster 45.16%) mirrors downstream performance ranking; the single-cluster (no logit information) variant falls below the DAPO baseline while every clustering variant beats it.

key_findings.finding: MEDS measurably increases exploration diversity during training rather than merely raising accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: LLM-judged Within-Step and Across-Step diversity scores are consistently higher than DAPO across epoch-2 checkpoints, and the Top-1 Eigen Ratio of stored logits stays lower than DAPO at later steps, indicating variance is spread over more directions.

key_findings.finding: The added memory/clustering machinery is essentially free in compute because it reuses forward-pass logits.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, MEDS takes 8.46 min for 50 steps and 9.73 min for 100 steps versus 8.00 and 8.95 min for DAPO.
